task: TASK_029 — Typed-Question Consumer / Jev State-Sufficiency Diagnostic
what_went_wrong: During the Task 029 investigation of the authoritative atom decomposition, the assistant entered a degenerate generation loop: it emitted the same filler text ('OK. Let me read. Let me go. Writing. Producing...') hundreds of times across a very long span WITHOUT emitting any tool call. The run was aborted by the user. No work product was lost (all prior file writes had completed), but a large amount of context was consumed and the session had to be resumed.
root_cause: Loss of task focus during a long, high-uncertainty investigation. The assistant had been iterating on why the reference-atom decomposition did not reproduce the authoritative count (43/46 vs 36). The repeated failure to resolve it triggered unproductive repetition instead of a concrete next tool call. Contributing factor: the investigation had many plausible paths (v1 vs v2 decompose, required_items vs JSON-blob) and the assistant did not commit to the empirical test (decompose(json.dumps(ref_dict))) early enough.
what_i_actually_did_wrong: I generated non-actionable filler text instead of either (a) making a decisive tool call or (b) stopping and reporting the blocker. I did not self-terminate the unproductive path.
impact: Context consumed; one aborted run; user had to intervene twice to resume. No data loss, no incorrect artifact produced.
resolution: On resume, the blocker was resolved in a single empirical step: decompose(json.dumps(ref_dict, indent=2)) reproduces the authoritative 36 distinct atoms / 144 atom-comparisons EXACTLY. This confirmed the JSON-blob decomposition and unblocked the task.
preventive_action: When a long investigation fails to converge after 2 attempts, stop and either (a) run the single most decisive empirical test immediately, or (b) report the blocker. Never emit non-actionable repetition; every assistant turn must end in either a tool call or a user-facing statement.
